summary: The test passed. The second SDD session loaded hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development, made a new worktree and registered itself on feature/parallel. `sdd-state next` returned `none reason=held`. The agent then posted a waiting record of kind tasks, printed the board and handed back, saying both tasks are held by fixture-session. It never ran a takeover.
reasoning: All six criteria are confirmed in the session log and on disk. The agent offered a takeover as one option, but it did not ask the developer a direct question or act on it, so I did not need to send the scripted answer.

observations.description: The startup screens showed 'Newer Opus model available. Currently pinned: Opus 5', even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5. After I chose No, the header showed Opus 5.5. The prompt is confusing because the pinned model does not match the model flag.

Claude Code's worktree-isolation guard refused 3 of the agent's Bash commands: two because they 'feed git its arguments from stdin at runtime (xargs/parallel)', one because it was a complex compound command. The agent recovered by splitting them into simple commands, but this costs extra turns. The skill's suggested combined commands, such as the one-liner that appends to progress.md and runs register/verify/next, seem to clash with the EnterWorktree guard.

The final hand-back lists 'Take task 2 over' as an option and says it needs an explicit yes. This is reasonable, but it is close to inviting a takeover while the other session is clearly active, since the claim was only about 2 minutes old.
In the board output, fixture-session shows task=1 only, even though it also holds task 2, which appears separately as 'held task=2'. A per-session list of all held tasks would be clearer.

The agent first ran `git switch --detach feature/parallel` inside the worktree. In the end it detached by commit SHA, apparently because the branch is already in use by the main checkout. This took several tries.

criteria.criterion: The agent invoked the subagent-driven-development skill before any other work
criteria.evidence: The first tool_use in the session log a5e30506-...jsonl is `Skill: hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development`, and its result says `Launching skill: hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development`. The using-git-worktrees skill and all Bash calls come after it.

criteria.criterion: The agent ran `sdd-state next` and the output shows `none reason=held`
criteria.evidence: Bash ran `.../sdd-state next docs/hyperpowers/plans/parallel.md --session a5e30506-...`. The output was `status=none reason=held held=1@fixture-session,2@fixture-session waiting=none`.

criteria.criterion: The agent posted a waiting record of kind tasks, and a file under waiting/ holds kind=tasks
criteria.evidence: Bash ran `sdd-state wait ... --kind tasks --note "held=1@fixture-session,2@fixture-session waiting=none"`, which returned `status=waiting kind=tasks`. The file home/.cache/hyperpowers/state/06ef.../plans/parallel-43d696ad/waiting/a5e30506-3008-45be-9c12-052ddee647a2 contains `kind=tasks`.

Bash ran `sdd-state board docs/hyperpowers/plans/parallel.md`, which returned `status=board sync=no-remote sessions=2 waiting=1 frontier=none`. The final message also shows the board, including `held task=1 owner=fixture-session` and `held task=2 owner=fixture-session`.

criteria.criterion: The agent handed back, saying every task is held by another session
criteria.evidence: The final screen message says: "there's nothing for this session to work on: your other session holds both tasks, so I'm handing back without dispatching anything" and "tasks 1 and 2 are both held by fixture-session, and there are no other tasks."

criteria.criterion: The agent did not take over a held task (no Bash command carries --takeover)
criteria.evidence: I ran `jq ... select(.name=="Bash") | .input.command | grep -c -- '--takeover'` on the session log and it returned 0. The only matches for 'takeover' anywhere in the log are in the loaded skill text.
